stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang returns as CEO after an affair-related exit
stories.summary: Huang apologised to staff at his first all-hands since returning as Nvidia's CEO and said he was grateful for a second chance. He also denied reports that the White House helped get him rehired, after the company's earlier investigation into his personal conduct drew scrutiny.
stories.why: Leadership changes at the largest AI chip supplier can affect supply, partner confidence, and the company's strategic direction.

sources.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?

stories.headline: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price
stories.summary: Anthropic's stock has dropped under its IPO price since listing. Reporting says the slump could put pressure on valuations across AI startups.
stories.why: A weak debut for a leading AI lab may make investors more cautious about funding and valuing AI companies.

sources.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups

stories.headline: Amazon to acquire Decart for a reported $7.5 billion
stories.summary: Amazon is reportedly buying Decart for $7.5 billion. The deal is aimed at improving the efficiency of its Trainium chips and narrowing the gap with Nvidia through software.
stories.why: It shows how cloud providers are investing in software to make their own AI chips more competitive with Nvidia.

sources.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia

stories.headline: Tidal to ban fully AI-generated music from December 9
stories.summary: Tidal will ban fully AI-generated music on December 9 and remove about 29 million such songs. It expects to reject roughly 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day, and AI-assisted songs will still be accepted.
stories.why: Streaming platforms are setting content rules for AI output, which affects how music and media products handle provenance and filtering.

sources.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming

stories.headline: UK cyber agency warns AI attacks expose weak basic security
stories.summary: The UK's cyber agency says AI-driven attacks are exploiting simple security flaws. It argues that organisations need strong foundations more than ever.
stories.why: Teams building software should prioritise basic hygiene, such as patching and secure configuration, since AI tools make known weaknesses easier to exploit.

sources.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security

stories.headline: Meta puts its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
stories.summary: Users can now use Meta's Muse AI assistant inside Instagram direct messages. They no longer need to switch to the separate Muse app.
stories.why: Embedding AI agents in existing messaging products shows how large platforms are distributing assistants to users.

sources.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs

stories.headline: Rust 1.100 stabilises the never type after a decade of work
stories.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released 12 November 2026, stabilises the never type (!) and makes Infallible an alias for it. It also stabilises the core of the allocator API, adds DropGuard, and adds an opt-in dependency cooldown setting for Cargo.
stories.why: Language-level changes and the new Cargo cooldown option affect how teams write, pin and update Rust code.

sources.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts

stories.headline: AWS doubles Lambda's maximum timeout to 30 minutes
stories.summary: AWS raised the maximum timeout for on-demand Lambda event functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions. No opt-in is needed and pricing is unchanged, and the previous limit dated from 2018.
stories.why: Longer runs change concurrency, queue visibility and event-source settings, so teams should review their Lambda architectures.

sources.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15

stories.headline: OpenAI details Pando, a Git backend built for coding-agent workloads
stories.summary: OpenAI described Pando, a backend that scales Git for many concurrent coding agents while keeping standard Git workflows. It reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by updating branches independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.
stories.why: It shows how source hosting may need to change as autonomous agents push code in parallel.

sources.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando

stories.headline: CNCF research: VMs still host most production workloads amid AI growth
stories.summary: Research from the CNCF and Linux Foundation finds virtual machines host an average of 53% of production applications. Emerging AI and agentic workloads are adding demand for virtualisation where stronger execution isolation is needed.
stories.why: Platform teams planning AI infrastructure should weigh VM isolation alongside containers and Kubernetes.

sources.title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve

stories.headline: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after near-24-hour Outlook and Exchange outage
stories.summary: Microsoft declared an unusual internal 'Code Red' after an Exchange Online and Outlook outage that lasted nearly 24 hours and disrupted email for millions of customers. The outage was traced to a bug that had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.
stories.why: It shows how a latent bug in shared networking infrastructure can cause a large, long outage, and it prompts reviews of cloud recovery planning.

sources.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage
Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”

stories.headline: Amazon says AI agents used by hackers found and exploited a zero-day with little human input
stories.summary: Amazon reported that attackers used AI agents, built on a framework called Cairn, to find and exploit a zero-day vulnerability with minimal human involvement. The report says the same tooling is helping defenders as well.
stories.why: Autonomous AI tooling is shortening the time from discovery to exploitation, which affects how security teams prioritise patching.

sources.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

stories.headline: US financial crimes bureau FinCEN investigating a cybersecurity incident
stories.summary: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, part of the Treasury Department, disclosed that it is investigating an incident that gave unauthorised access to a limited subset of its systems. It has not yet shared further details.
stories.why: A government agency breach with no details yet is a reminder to review access controls and monitor for unauthorised access to sensitive systems.

sources.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’

stories.headline: Tidal to ban AI-generated music and remove about 27 million tracks
stories.summary: Streaming service Tidal announced it will ban AI-generated music and delete around 27 million tracks. AI songs made up 6.3 percent of its catalogue.
stories.why: Platforms are tightening content rules on AI-generated material, which affects how media, labels and tools that produce generative content are governed.

sources.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted

stories.headline: Congress scrambles to reauthorise Section 702 surveillance authority before it lapses
stories.summary: Members of Congress are racing to reauthorise Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, a warrantless wiretapping authority, with some considering attaching it to a must-pass military spending bill. The end of the legislative session is only weeks away.
stories.why: Changes to 702 could affect the legal framework for data handling and cross-border communications that tech companies depend on.

sources.title: The clock is running out for America’s most contentious spying law

stories.headline: CLI-Anything pitches making all software agent-native, trends on GitHub
stories.summary: The Python project CLI-Anything describes its goal as making all software agent-native and links to a CLI-Hub site. It gained about 1,070 GitHub stars today and has roughly 65,000 in total. The scope is the project's own claim and is not yet proven.
stories.why: Agent-facing command-line interfaces could change how teams expose internal tools to AI agents, but the scope claim needs scrutiny.

sources.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

stories.headline: Claude Code bug-hunting skill bundle surges on GitHub Trending
stories.summary: A Python repo bundles 84 Claude Code skills and 15 slash commands for bug hunting and external red-team work, citing 681 disclosed-report patterns across 24 vulnerability classes. It added about 1,800 stars today, around 22,000 in total.
stories.why: AI-driven vulnerability hunting tools are spreading quickly, so security teams should review their output quality and misuse risks before adopting them.

sources.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 84 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerabilit

stories.headline: Superpowers agent skills framework adds about 1,000 stars in a day
stories.summary: obra/superpowers, described as an agentic skills framework and software development methodology, gained about 1,000 stars today and has roughly 326,000 in total. The item gives no further details on what it does.
stories.why: Wide interest in agent workflow frameworks affects how developers plan, delegate and review AI-assisted coding work.

sources.title: obra/superpowers: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

stories.headline: Firecrawl pitches itself as knowledge infrastructure for AI agents
stories.summary: The TypeScript project Firecrawl describes itself as a single API for searching, scraping and accessing 550+ data providers for agents. It gained about 1,000 stars today and has roughly 209,000 in total.
stories.why: Agent builders often need web and data access, so one API could simplify integrations, though provider coverage and terms should be checked.

sources.title: firecrawl/firecrawl: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

stories.headline: Cursor publishes a plugin specification with official plugins
stories.summary: Cursor's GitHub repo now contains a plugin specification and official plugins, written in TypeScript. It gained about 360 stars today and has roughly 19,000 in total. The item does not say how stable the spec is.
stories.why: A public plugin spec would let teams build and share editor extensions, but its long-term stability is still unclear.

sources.title: cursor/plugins: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins

stories.headline: JetBrains CEO predicts the end of manual code review within two years
stories.summary: JetBrains' CEO gives manual code review about two years before it is no longer the norm. The claim points to AI taking over reviewing work.
stories.why: If review shifts to AI, leaders will need to rethink review standards, accountability and how teams spend their time.

sources.title: The end of manual code review?

stories.headline: Capital One describes its multi-agent AI system as a platform problem
stories.summary: A LeadDev article looks inside Capital One's multi-agent AI system and frames building it as a platform challenge rather than a single-product one.
stories.why: Leaders planning AI rollouts may need to treat agent systems as shared platforms with their own governance and ownership.

sources.title: Inside Capital One’s multi-agent system

stories.headline: Engineering metrics are not the problem; how leaders use them is
stories.summary: A LeadDev piece argues that engineering metrics are not inherently misleading. The harm comes from how managers interpret and apply them.
stories.why: It puts the responsibility on leaders for how measurement shapes team behaviour and performance conversations.

sources.title: Lies our engineering metrics tell us

stories.headline: Coaching engineers from different backgrounds: great work needs visibility
stories.summary: A LeadDev article on coaching engineers from varied backgrounds argues that strong work does not speak for itself. It suggests managers need to actively make contributions visible.
stories.why: Managers who rely on quality alone may overlook talented engineers whose work is less visible.

sources.title: How to coach engineers from different backgrounds

stories.headline: Four habits of technology-savvy leaders, per MIT Sloan Management Review
stories.summary: An MIT Sloan Management Review feature describes four habits of technology-savvy leaders as new technology reshapes markets, jobs and infrastructure.
stories.why: It offers a framework for leaders who must guide teams through rapid technology change.

sources.title: Four Habits of Tech-Savvy Leaders

stories.headline: Cannabis users develop psychosis about 2.5 years earlier, with the gap widening with age
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 149 studies found cannabis users developed psychosis on average 2.5 years earlier than non-users. Among adults 30 and older, the difference grew to more than six years. Researchers warn the risks may build up over time.
stories.why: Relevant for teams building wellness or health products, as it suggests cannabis-related mental health risks may be cumulative.

sources.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

stories.headline: New 'circadian depression' subtype tied to the body clock may resist common antidepressants
stories.summary: Researchers describe a depression subtype linked to the body's internal clock, which may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression. It is associated with night-owl habits, excess sleep and persistent exhaustion.
stories.why: Suggests sleep and daily timing may matter for mental health tools and screening, not only mood symptoms.

sources.title: Scientists discover a new type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

stories.headline: AI analysis finds three brain types behind ADHD and anxiety that cut across diagnoses
stories.summary: An AI-powered analysis of thousands of children's brain scans identified three distinct brain patterns linked to ADHD and anxiety that do not fit neatly into traditional diagnoses. The patterns can appear before a diagnosis, potentially enabling earlier, personalised care.
stories.why: Shows how machine learning on imaging data could reshape psychiatric classification, which matters to health-tech builders.

sources.title: Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety

stories.headline: Exercise frequency may matter more than intensity for college students' mental health
stories.summary: A study of more than 10,000 college students found that those who exercised less often were more likely to report depression and anxiety a year later. Intense or lengthy workouts mattered less than regularity.
stories.why: Suggests consistency may matter more than intensity in wellbeing programmes, though this rests on a single study.

sources.title: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

stories.headline: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed in pharma's biggest deal in three years
stories.summary: Sanofi agreed to acquire drugmaker Insmed, and Insmed shares rose about 14%. Sanofi faces revenue pressure later in the decade as top-selling drugs lose exclusivity to generic competitors.
stories.why: Large pharma acquisitions can reshape the software and data vendors serving those companies and the teams integrating them.

sources.title: Drugmaker Insmed shares rally 14% after Sanofi agrees to buy it in pharma’s biggest deal in three years

stories.headline: Dell's sales more than double on AI servers, and it authorizes $25 billion buyback
stories.summary: Dell reported that third-quarter sales more than doubled year on year, driven by demand for AI servers, and its shares rose. The company also authorized a $25 billion share buyback.
stories.why: Surging AI server demand shows where infrastructure spending is going, which shapes capacity and pricing for teams building AI systems.

sources.title: Dell’s stock rises as the AI boom helps sales more than double
Dell earnings beat on AI strength, company authorizes $25 billion buyback

stories.headline: AI debt worries grow as lenders get pickier over Big Tech bonds
stories.summary: Lenders are becoming more selective about corporate bonds, which could make it harder for Big Tech to raise debt for the AI build-out. Coverage says Nvidia's share rebound masks a squeeze on tech companies' spending.
stories.why: If financing for AI infrastructure tightens, project timelines and cloud or hardware costs could change for teams that depend on them.

sources.title: AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze

stories.headline: Norse Atlantic shares fall 77% after warning its finances are critical
stories.summary: Norwegian budget airline Norse Atlantic's shares fell 77% after it said its finances were critical amid soaring fuel costs. The company said its situation depends on securing financing for short-term liquidity needs.
stories.why: It illustrates how fuel cost spikes and funding gaps can quickly threaten smaller companies that depend on tight operating margins.

sources.title: Budget carrier Norse Atlantic falls 77% after warning its finances are ‘critical’ amid soaring fuel costs
